# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 52 (Bi-Vb Pc52)

**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 52
**Title (English, from literature):** Abusing a monk

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Although the nuns plot retaliation against Kappitaka, Upāli foils the murder plot, leading the nuns to verbally abuse Upāli instead [Hüsken 1997]. In the non-offense clause (*anāpatti*), an exemption is provided for a nun whose harsh words occur in the course of explaining, commenting upon, or reciting the Dhamma [Hüsken 1997].
Scholars note that the rule of Pācittiya 52 is textually identical to the seventh of the eight "weighty rules" (*garudhammā*) found in the Cullavagga [Hüsken 1997]. Ute Hüsken points out an internal legal contradiction within the Theravāda Vinaya: whereas an infraction of the seventh *garudhamma* is treated on par with a *saṅghādisesa* requiring a fourteen-day penance (*mānatta*), Pācittiya 52 requires only simple confession [Hüsken 1997].
